instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company has an IAM role in its production account for reading reports from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same account. Developers in the company's development account must use the role. Their IAM policies allow sts:AssumeRole on the role ARN. When a developer calls AssumeRole, the call fails with an access denied error. Which change will fix the problem with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Update the permissions policy of the role so that it allows s3:GetObject on the report bucket and on the objects in it.

options.label: B
options.text: Update the trust policy of the role in the production account so that it names the development account as a principal.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an IAM user in the production account for each developer, with an access key and read access to the bucket.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a bucket policy to the report bucket that allows s3:GetObject for the development account as the principal.

items.stem: A company runs an order-processing application on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The application reads and writes objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. Company policy requires that no long-term credentials are stored where the application runs. The company also runs a private certificate authority that issues certificates to its servers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Move the application to new Amazon EC2 instances, and attach an IAM role to the new instances through an instance profile.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach an IAM role through an instance profile, and let the AWS SDK load the temporary credentials from the instance metadata.

options.label: C
options.text: Use IAM Roles Anywhere with certificates from the private certificate authority, and exchange each certificate for temporary role credentials.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an IAM user for the application, store its access key in an encrypted file where the application runs, and rotate it monthly.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has 40 member accounts. About 300 employees need access to the AWS Management Console and the AWS CLI in several accounts, based on their job functions. The company has no external identity provider. The security team wants to centrally manage which employees can access each account, and employees must use one sign-in to reach all their accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable IAM Identity Center, create the employees as users and groups in its identity store, and assign permission sets to the groups for each account.

options.label: B
options.text: Create IAM users in one central account, and let the users switch to roles that the security team creates in each member account.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool for the employees, and map each group in the user pool to an IAM role in every member account.

options.label: D
options.text: Create IAM users for the employees in each member account, add the users to IAM groups by job function, and attach policies to each group.

items.stem: A company is building a mobile app that lets each user upload photos directly to an Amazon S3 bucket. Users sign up and sign in to the app through an Amazon Cognito user pool. The company expects the app to grow quickly. Company policy requires that the app does not contain long-term AWS credentials. Each upload must use temporary credentials. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a user in IAM Identity Center for each app user, and let the app request credentials for a permission set that allows uploads.

options.label: B
options.text: Use an Amazon Cognito identity pool to give each signed-in user temporary credentials for an IAM role that allows s3:PutObject on the bucket.

options.label: C
options.text: Use an Amazon Cognito identity pool to give each signed-in user temporary credentials for an IAM role that allows all Amazon S3 actions.

options.label: D
options.text: Call the AWS STS GetFederationToken operation from the app for each user, and pass a session policy that allows uploads to the bucket.

items.stem: A company runs an order-processing application on servers in the company's data center. The application reads and writes objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. Company policy requires that no long-term credentials are stored where the application runs. The company also runs a private certificate authority that issues certificates to its servers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Use IAM Roles Anywhere with certificates from the private certificate authority, and exchange each certificate for temporary role credentials.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach an IAM role through an instance profile, and let the AWS SDK load the temporary credentials from the instance metadata.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an IAM user for the application, store its access key in an encrypted file where the application runs, and rotate it monthly.

options.label: D
options.text: Move the application to new Amazon EC2 instances, and attach an IAM role to the new instances through an instance profile.

items.stem: A company manages its own keys in AWS KMS. An application on Amazon EC2 instances uses an IAM role to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same account. The objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS and a customer managed key. The role's IAM policy allows s3:GetObject on the bucket and kms:Decrypt on the key. The key policy has one statement, which allows the key administrators' IAM role to use and manage the key. Every read fails with an access denied error. Which solution will fix the reads with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a statement to the key policy that allows the application's IAM role to use kms:Decrypt on the key, and keep the IAM policy unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to the application's IAM role, so that its identity-based policy allows every AWS KMS action on the key.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new customer managed key with the default key policy, re-encrypt every object with the new key, and schedule the old key for deletion.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows s3:GetObject and kms:Decrypt for the application's IAM role on the bucket and the key.

items.stem: A company runs a batch application on AWS Lambda. During testing, a developer attached the AdministratorAccess policy to the function's execution role. The application has now run in production for two months, and an AWS CloudTrail trail records the account's activity. The security team must replace the policy with a policy that follows the principle of least privilege and that matches the actions the function really uses. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Read two months of CloudTrail log files by hand, list every action that the role called, and write a customer managed policy from the list.

options.label: B
options.text: Download the IAM credential report, find the services that the role used, and write a customer managed policy that allows those services.

options.label: C
options.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate a policy from the role's CloudTrail activity, review the generated policy, and attach it in place of AdministratorAccess.

options.label: D
options.text: Run the IAM policy simulator for each AWS action against the role, and keep in a new policy the actions that the simulator allows.

items.stem: A company has a new AWS account. Two founders share the password of the root user and sign in as the root user every day to launch Amazon EC2 instances and to edit IAM policies. A deployment script on an EC2 instance uses an access key of the root user. An auditor asks the company to protect the root user and to follow AWS security best practices. Which action should the company take?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on MFA for the root user, and keep using the root user and its access key for daily administration and for the script.

options.label: B
options.text: Set a permissions boundary on the root user that allows only Amazon EC2 and IAM actions, and keep the access key for the script.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep the root user for daily work, rotate its access key every month, and store the new key in an encrypted file on the instance.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on MFA for the root user, delete its access key, and do the daily work and the script through identities that use IAM roles.

items.stem: A company stores customer records in Amazon S3 buckets and Amazon DynamoDB tables. Employees in three teams need different access to the records. A new compliance officer lists the security tasks for this workload and asks which tasks belong to the company under the AWS shared responsibility model. The company wants to assign an owner in the company to each of its own tasks. Which task is the responsibility of the company?

options.label: A
options.text: Granting each team the IAM permissions that it needs on the buckets and the tables

options.label: B
options.text: Patching the operating system of the hosts that run the Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB services

options.label: C
options.text: Updating the platform software that runs the Amazon DynamoDB service with the latest security fixes

options.label: D
options.text: Protecting the data center buildings and the network hardware that run the storage services

items.stem: A company has 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Employees sign in with user accounts in an Active Directory domain in the company's data center. The employees must use their existing Active Directory credentials to access the AWS accounts. The company does not want to run a second directory in AWS or to keep copies of the passwords in AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create IAM users in each AWS account with a script that copies the user names from Active Directory, and require MFA for each IAM user.

options.label: B
options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector as the identity source, and assign permission sets to Active Directory groups for the AWS accounts.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure SAML 2.0 federation from an AD FS server in the data center to an IAM identity provider and IAM roles in each AWS account.

options.label: D
options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, and create a trust relationship with the on-premises domain.

items.stem: A company's administrators use the AWS CLI with the access keys of their IAM users to manage objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. Their IAM policy allows all Amazon S3 actions on the bucket. Each administrator already has an MFA device registered to the IAM user. A new security rule requires that a request to delete an object succeeds only after the administrator authenticates with the MFA device. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Have each administrator call AWS STS GetSessionToken with an MFA code, and use the temporary credentials that it returns for delete requests.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep signing delete requests with the access keys, because the MFA devices that are registered to the IAM users add MFA status to each key.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new IAM role that allows s3:DeleteObject and requires MFA in its trust policy, and remove s3:DeleteObject from the administrators' IAM policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the IAM policy so that it allows s3:DeleteObject on the bucket only when the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition key is true.

options.label: E
options.text: Turn on S3 MFA Delete on the bucket so that each administrator's IAM user must enter an MFA code to delete an object.

items.stem: A company uses a third-party monitoring service that runs in the vendor's own AWS account. The vendor needs read-only access to the configuration of resources in the company's AWS account. The vendor serves many customers and gives each customer a unique ID for this connection. The security team must prevent other customers of the vendor from using the vendor to reach the company's account. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST securely? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create an IAM role whose trust policy names the vendor's AWS account as the principal, and attach a read-only permissions policy to the role.

options.label: B
options.text: Choose one external ID value in the company, and give the same value to every vendor that assumes a role in the company's account.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an IAM user for the vendor with a read-only policy, and send the vendor the access key of the user through an encrypted channel.

options.label: D
options.text: Put the read-only actions in the trust policy of the role, so that the vendor's account can assume the role and read the configuration.

options.label: E
options.text: Add a condition to the trust policy of the role that requires the sts:ExternalId value that the vendor generated for the company.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations and runs workloads in three AWS Regions. The security team must audit which Amazon S3 buckets, AWS KMS keys, and IAM roles in the member accounts allow access from principals outside the organization. The team wants a new finding to appear when a policy change shares a resource outside the organization. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create one IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust in the Region where the security team works.

options.label: B
options.text: Run AWS Lambda functions in each Region that read every resource policy daily and report each statement that names an outside principal.

options.label: C
options.text: Generate the IAM credential report in each member account every day, and review which users and access keys can reach the resources.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust in each of the three Regions.

items.stem: A company has an IAM role in its production account for reading reports from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same account. Developers in the company's development account must use the role. Their IAM policies allow sts:AssumeRole on the role ARN. When a developer calls AssumeRole, the call succeeds, but the next call to read a report fails with an access denied error. Which change will fix the problem with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a bucket policy to the report bucket that allows s3:GetObject for the development account as the principal.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an IAM user in the production account for each developer, with an access key and read access to the bucket.

options.label: C
options.text: Update the trust policy of the role in the production account so that it names the development account as a principal.

options.label: D
options.text: Update the permissions policy of the role so that it allows s3:GetObject on the report bucket and on the objects in it.
